text:
eval-bot: nightly-evals: model=rwd-v2-quant-int4 run_id=nightly-2026-03-19 failed 4/120 prompts (multilang/zh). Alerting thread.
liao: saw this pop. quick summary?
eval-bot: failures concentrated on multilang/zh translation suite — outputs switching to pinyin or inserting ASCII name tokens for 3 prompts, plus punctuation collapse for others.
chen: repro locally with the nightly docker + int4 profile. failing prompt sample: "翻译: 我刚见到王小明，他说他会晚点到" -> model outputs "I just met Wang Xiaoming, he said he'd be late" (pinyin) instead of Chinese.
akiko: that's wild — model should keep target script zh-Hans. Any config drift in tokenizer or special tokens?
liao: checked tokenizer hash used in serving: `tok-v1.3` unchanged. But quantization pipeline changed kernel selection yesterday (fused-gemm-int4). Could be KV cache or detokenization bug.
matt: attaching small diff from greedy decode between fp16 and int4: ```- fp16: "我刚见到王小明，他说他会晚点到。"+ int4: "I just met Wang Xiaoming, he said he'd be late"```
chen: another failing case shows partial romaji on names inside longer zh paragraphs. Looks like ID for CJK char class incorrectly mapped to fallback alphabet in int4 decoder path.
akiko: are there any failing examples in zh-tw or only zh-cn?
liao: mainly zh-Hans prompts, but we saw 1 zh-Hant prompt where punctuation got stripped and sentence split across lines.
sre-oncall: any impact on customer-facing hosted models? rollout for rwd-v2-quant-int4 is limited to internal nightly only, no prod traffic. Dedicated clusters still on fp16.
matt: I ran a quick bisect across commits: the kernel selection change at commit `4f9d2b` (yesterday) correlates exactly with regression. Reverting that kernel selection in inference binary restores fp-like outputs.
chen: plan: gate int4 fused kernel until we audit symbol->token mapping in detokenizer + add targeted regression tests for CJK character class (names, punctuation, mixed ASCII).
akiko: add prompt set to nightly that includes mixed-script names and embedded ASCII (emails, urls) — we need to ensure we don't fallback to ascii for CJK.
sre-oncall: I'll hold the canary so no further internal rollouts. Also scheduling postmortem if this makes it to staging.
liao: can someone open a short PR with testcases + revert patch? I'll own verification.
matt: opening PR now: https://git.redwood.internal/r/inf/kerndefaults/pull/142 — includes failing examples and a test that asserts no ASCII tokens in pure-zh outputs.
akiko: also add a metric in Redwood Console: percent of CJK prompts that produce any Latin letters other than accepted romanization tokens (pinyin flag).
chen: adding a short note to onboarding checklist: when adding quant kernels, run script `tests/ml/locale_token_smoke.py` against a representative prompt set.
sre-oncall: thanks. tagging security/ops just in case: @security @ops — low severity but tracking. :white_check_mark:
